checks.label: recording
checks.heading: Block chords, then Revoice
checks.text:
Block chords, then Revoice

Harmony Off keeps each chord in its written root-position voicing. Revoice moves those same chord notes to different octaves while preserving their pitch classes, note count and rhythm; ROOT keeps each chord root lowest.

Your starting point: Use a separate empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and C major. Assign Doubledecker to channel 1, range 1–16. Set Note MIDI 48, Vel 80, Len 2 steps, Chd1=3rd and Chd2=5th; add trigs at 1,5,9,13 and root notes MIDI 48,45,53,55 (C, A, F, G).

Build this example
Before: build slot 1 at length 32 with Harmony Mode Off. It plays C, A minor, F and G in root position on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 of each bar. Play twice to hear the written voicing.
After: copy slot 1 to slot 2 and select slot 2; keep length 32. Open Channel tasks > Harmony. Select Mode with E2, choose REVOICE with E3 and press K3. Select Register with E2 and press K3; select Bass Mode with E2, choose ROOT with E3 and apply as the page indicates.
Compare bars 1-2 with bars 3-4: the same four chords, notes and rhythm return, but some notes move to other octaves and each chord root is lowest. Play both slots, then Stop and select slot 1 to restore Harmony Off.
Restore your starting point
Select slot 1 to restore Harmony Off, then stop and return to the separate course project.
Listen
Block chords, then Revoice

Doubledecker on channel 1 plays a four-chord progression, C, A minor, F and G in C major, on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 of every bar for four bars at 90 BPM, as triads at velocity 80 with Chd1 on the 3rd and Chd2 on the 5th, each chord two steps long. In the first two bars Harmony is Off, so the chords sound exactly as written, each in root position. In the last two bars Harmony Revoice is on. It keeps the same chords, with the same pitch classes, number of notes and rhythm, and only re-places the notes in other octaves, with each chord's root lowest. Listen for the same four chords being re-voiced at bar 3, about 5.3 seconds in, while the harmony stays the same.

This is the original recording. Follow the build and listening notes alongside it.

CH 1 / Doubledecker
Listen for
At bar 3, the same four pitch-class groups and rhythm return in different octaves, with each chord root lowest.

MIDI Keyboard Input

Hold a step to enter it, or arm recording and play.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Select channel; Record off; no step held; play MIDI keys	Audition the selected channel’s output without entering step masks.
Select channel → hold step → play MIDI keys	Enter that step’s note, velocity and chord masks.
Record (2,8) + running transport + MIDI keys	Record onto the selected channel’s active steps.
Norns Menu Navigation

Open tasks with E1; choose a row with E2 and change its value with E3.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
E1 → E2 → K3	Open the context task list, select a task, then open it.
E2 / E3	Select a row / change its value.
K3 / K2 on staged settings	Apply the draft / cancel or return. K3 also confirms a question and K2 cancels it. While an OPEN > row is chosen the last line names the target, for example K3 OPEN RHYTHM, or just K3 OPEN when space is short.
Hold K1 + E3	Change the selected value finely where it supports that.
